items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Louis Nash was the drummer. ... We played that night

ctx.x: You played with Dizzy just before he passed. I imagine that must have been . . .

Yeah. It was disturbing, too. He had two weeks at the – I think two weeks at the Blue Note in New York, and he had a different group each night. The night I played, it was David Sanchez – the tenor player – me, and Dizzy of course, and I don’t remember. Louis Nash was the drummer. That’s right. I don’t remember who the other people was. We played that night, and then he played the other nights with somebody else. He wasn’t the Diz that he was when he was at his peak. He was ailing. That’s the last time I ever…
